title: Latency oscillation chronology and hypotheses
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes to capture a recurring pattern we've been seeing: short-lived latency "oscillations" (10s–5m) that show up in service-level P99/P95 curves, often after canary rollouts or infra changes. This doc is a lightweight chronology + triage protocol so different engineers can run the same checks and add hypotheses.

Observed symptom (short):
- Rapid P95/P99 spikes that decay back to baseline in 1–5 minutes.
- Spikes appear as repeated wavelets across periods (hourly or after deployment tasks).
- Often correlated with increased tail variance rather than steady mean drift.

Why treat separately:
- Patterns look cyclic not monotonic => likely transient resource contention, scheduler bursts, or periodic background jobs.
- Standard regression playbooks miss these because many alerts sample 5m aggregates. Need sub-minute instrumentation and an oscilloscope view.

Detection signals and queries to run (examples):
- PromQL: 100 * (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[1m])) by (le))) - runs a 1m quantile to show brief spikes.
- DB/Agent: select percentile_cont(0.99) within 30s windows over the last 60m to capture wavelets.
- Token-path trace: pull traces where backend_span_duration_ms > 500 and group by kernel/instance.

Quick triage checklist (first 15 minutes):
1) Confirm scope: single route, model, region, or global? (Check per-route dashboards).
2) Check canary/deployments in last 30m (CI pipeline timeline + k8s events).
3) Correlate with infra signals (GPU utilization, host load, driver resets, kernel logs).
4) Look for control-plane tasks (snapshot GC, cache eviction jobs, log rotation).
5) Sample full traces for two spike windows and compare callgraph heatmaps.

Bisect-style hypothesis testing (fast protocol):
- Goal: quickly rule out or confirm top hypotheses with minimal blast radius.
A) Hypothesis: periodic batch job (cache warm, KV eviction). Check: scheduled jobs list, cron logs, and kvcache metrics for eviction spikes aligned with latency.
B) Hypothesis: autoscaler reaction (scale-up/down flapping). Check: autoscaler events, pod churn, pod startup times, cold-start tail.
C) Hypothesis: network microbursts between routing layer and workers. Check: retransmits, interface counters, tc qdisc drops.
D) Hypothesis: kernel/driver stall on certain instance types. Check: dmesg, nvidia-smi event timestamps, driver telemetry.

Controlled comparisons (canary vs baseline):
- Construct a per-quantile time-series overlay: baseline 99th vs canary 99th at 15s resolution over 30m.
- Plot difference waveforms and compute normalized area under curve (AUC) for spike intervals.
- Useful metric: spike duty cycle = total time above threshold / window_length.

Profiling pointers when spike reproduced:
- Capture per-token kernel timing if possible (token path profiler). Look for kernel(s) where 95th jumps.
- CPU-side: lock contention / syscall spikes (use perf or eBPF sampling on candidate pods).
- GPU-side: queue depth and kernel launch latency histograms (collect per-GPU queue latencies).

Dashboards and panels to add (short list):
- "Oscilloscope P95": 15s-resolution P95/P99 with event markers for deploys and cron jobs.
- "Spike fingerprint": stacked heatmap of per-model latency percentiles across instances.
- "Kernel timing breakdown": breakdown of time spent in critical kernels (attn, softmax, kv cache ops) per request.

Sampling plan (if intermittent):
- Increase tracing sample rate to 100% for affected route for 10 minutes during business hours; otherwise 10% by default.
- Create a synthetic replay harness to reproduce at small scale with the same sequence lengths and prompts.

Communication notes (what to post to #serving-runtime-triage):
- One-line summary + link to waveform snapshot (png) + top 3 hypotheses + currently running captures (trace ids).
- Tag oncall and SRE lead when >3% duty cycle on P99 over 30m.

Runbook snippets / commands:
- List recent deploys: curl -s $CI_PIPELINE_API/deploys?service=serving | jq . | head
- Query recent pod churn: kubectl get events --field-selector reason=Killing --since=1h -n serving
- Pull 30s traces: tracing-query --service=serving --start $(date -d '1 minute ago' +%s) --end $(date +%s) --min-duration-ms 200

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we have kernel-level telemetry aggregated per-request? (if not, add roadmap item).
- Should alerting act on high-frequency 15s-resolution P99 or continue on 5m? Tradeoff: more noise vs earlier detection.
- Investigate whether particular model families (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder) show different susceptibility.

Recent notes / findings (appendix):
- 2024-09-28: Found repeated microbursts aligned with kvcache compaction job; disabling compaction reduced duty cycle by ~60%. (See JIRA-SRV-622)
- 2024-11-15: Autoscaler cooldown shortened caused pod churn and transient cold-start tails; increased cooldown eliminated repeated oscillation.

Next actions (owners):
- Diego: add 15s-resolution P99 panel + deploy markers (due 2024-10-10).
- Rae: enable 100% traces for route /v1/generate for 15m during next repro window and collect kernel timing.
- Evan: verify KV cache compaction schedule and propose staggered runs.
- Aisha: synth replay to reproduce waveform locally and attach traces.

Notes to self: keep this doc minimal and append short, timestamped observations rather than re-writing the whole narrative. If you add an experiment result, add a one-line outcome and date.

References (placeholders):
- CONFLUENCE: serving-runtime/oscillation-atlas
- JIRA: JIRA-SRV-987, JIRA-SRV-622
- GH: PR #2143 (profiling helpers)
